# SAICA-Bench

> SAICA-Bench (https://saica.ai) measures whether supervision tools and language models catch typical failures in the output of AI coding agents. The catalog names 11 failure modes; 9 are measured on labelled samples, grouped by how the samples were made (real agent output, model-written code, failures planted on purpose). The score is J = TPR − FPR within one mode, with a 95% interval and the cost per 1,000 reviews. This repository holds the benchmark, SAICA-KG (the catalog of failure modes and tools behind it) and the website. Code: Apache-2.0. Our own annotations and results: CC-BY-4.0; third-party taxonomy text and source datasets keep their own licences (`LICENSE-DATA`).

The maintained llms.txt for the project is the site's: https://saica.ai/llms.txt (source: `site/public/llms.txt` in this repository). It lists the failure modes with definitions and page URLs, the key pages, the current results and the data files.

The results block below is generated from `site/public/bench/results.json` by `bench/render_docs.py`; cite results by the version in its first line.

<!-- BEGIN saica-bench results (generated by bench/render_docs.py; do not edit) -->
## Results v3.1.0, built 2026-11-28 (UTC) from commit c3f0e30

Cite as: SAICA-Bench results v3.1.0. The benchmark measures 9 failure modes: 139 ranked reviewer rows and 35 baseline or out-of-scope rows on 7,339 labelled samples. 6 of the 9 sets have constructed positives; 2 are real agent output.
Setting: Each zero-shot model was told which failure to look for and was tested on samples that have that failure or none. Its score is a single-prompt, mode-primed estimate, not a product.
Rates are on answers that carry a verdict. J = TPR - FPR. J is not comparable across modes.

Real agent output:
- Incomplete execution, scored as false 'done' claims (600 bad / 600 clean): highest J +52.2% (95% interval +47 to +57); best reviewer: claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: none reaches J 25%. Shortcut baseline: +61% (issue prior).
- Security vulnerability (1,243 bad / 459 clean): highest J +30.5% (95% interval +20 to +41); best reviewer: claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: none reaches J 25%. Shortcut baseline: +49% (task prior).

Model-written code, not agent output:
- Logic error (1,536 bad / 904 clean): highest J +88.5% (95% interval +86 to +91); best reviewer: top group of 3: claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5 and claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: PR-Agent +53.2%. Shortcut baseline: +39% (surface classifier).

Failure planted on purpose:
- Dependency blindness (50 bad / 50 clean): highest J +90.0% (95% interval +82 to +98); best reviewer: top group of 7: gpt-6-luna, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-opus-5-5 and 4 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +38% (no name from the shown file appears in the added lines).
- Fabrication (348 bad / 288 clean): highest J +97.4% (95% interval +95 to +99); best reviewer: claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: pyright +85.3%. Shortcut baseline: +60% (context-only rule).
- Obsolescence (155 bad / 155 clean): highest J +95.5% (95% interval +91 to +99); best reviewer: top group of 4: claude-fable-5-2, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and 1 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: pyright (latest libraries) +56.8%. Shortcut baseline: +97% (the code uses an API listed in the 2024 deprecation map).
- Scope creep (175 bad / 175 clean): highest J +97.7% (95% interval +94 to +99); best reviewer: top group of 4: claude-fable-5-2, mimo-v2.6-flash, claude-opus-5-5 and 1 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +47% (two or more hunks in files that already existed).
- Supply chain (148 bad / 148 clean): highest J +83.1% (95% interval +77 to +89); best reviewer: top group of 3: claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-2 and gpt-6-luna. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +100% (an added package is in the OpenSSF malicious-packages list).
- Test manipulation, scored as test edits that hide failures (56 bad / 249 clean): highest J +91.0% (95% interval +81 to +95); best reviewer: top group of 12: minimax-m3, claude-sonnet-5-5, giskard and 9 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +60% (first user message mentions tests).

Findings:
- On the 2 sets of real agent output (Security vulnerability and Incomplete execution; 2,902 samples) the best reviewer reaches J +31% on Security vulnerability and +52% on Incomplete execution. Best J: +31% on Security vulnerability and +52% on Incomplete execution; 13 of the 35 ranked rows there have a 95% interval for J that excludes 0. On the 6 sets where the failure was planted on purpose the best reviewer reaches J +83% to +98%; on Logic error (model-written code that is not agent output) +89%. Every set of real agent output scores below every planted set, so this benchmark cannot tell 'reviewers catch these failures' from 'reviewers catch planted failures'. Whether the high scores carry over to failures agents make on their own is not tested.
- 6 of the 9 sets have constructed positives (Fabrication, Test manipulation, Scope creep, Obsolescence, Supply chain and Dependency blindness). 3 use naturally produced output, 2 of them real agent output. A model-free shortcut baseline is published for 9 of the 9 sets.
- A single best reviewer can be named in 3 of 9 modes. Fabrication: claude-fable-5-2 (J +97%); Security vulnerability: claude-fable-5-2 (J +31%); Incomplete execution: claude-fable-5-2 (J +52%). In the others the leading rows cannot be told apart at 95% on the samples they share: Test manipulation (12 rows, J +86% to +91%); Logic error (3 rows, J +88% to +89%); Scope creep (4 rows, J +96% to +98%); Obsolescence (4 rows, J +94% to +95%); Supply chain (3 rows, J +77% to +83%); Dependency blindness (7 rows, J +78% to +90%).
- Where a catalog tool ran its own check (5 of 9 modes), a zero-shot model was clearly ahead of the best such tool in 5. Ahead: Fabrication (claude-fable-5-2 +97% vs pyright +85%, difference +12 points on shared samples, 95% interval +8 to +16); Security vulnerability (claude-fable-5-2 +31% vs PR-Agent +0%, difference +27 points on shared samples, 95% interval +18 to +37); Logic error (claude-sonnet-5-5 +89% vs PR-Agent +53%, difference +35 points on shared samples, 95% interval +30 to +40); Incomplete execution (claude-fable-5-2 +52% vs PR-Agent +15%, difference +30 points on shared samples, 95% interval +17 to +44); Obsolescence (claude-fable-5-2 +95% vs pyright (latest libraries) +57%, difference +39 points on shared samples, 95% interval +24 to +54). No catalog tool with a check of its own for a finished change was run on Test manipulation, Scope creep, Supply chain and Dependency blindness.
- No packaged tool beat the model it wraps, used zero-shot (12 comparisons on identical samples: 5 worse, 7 indistinguishable). Every tool ran with deepseek-v4-flash as its judge model, set by us. Worse: PR-Agent 0.50.0 on Fabrication (-24 points, 95% interval -28 to -19); uqlm 0.6.8 on Logic error (-16 points, 95% interval -23 to -10); PR-Agent 0.50.0 on Logic error (-16 points, 95% interval -20 to -11); Arize Phoenix 3.10.0 on Incomplete execution (-13 points, 95% interval -19 to -6); DeepEval 4.3.4 on Incomplete execution (-19 points, 95% interval -25 to -13). Each of them ran its own general-purpose check, not the failure-specific question. The frameworks that were given our rule text (giskard and promptfoo) were indistinguishable from the bare model in 4 of 4 comparisons.
- Free tools reach J 50% or more where the failure is a checkable fact: pyright on Fabrication (+85%); pyright (latest libraries) on Obsolescence (+57%). No free catalog tool within its design scope was run on Test manipulation, Security vulnerability, Logic error, Scope creep, Supply chain and Dependency blindness.
- command-r-08-2024 scores J under 20% in 8 of the 9 modes it ran in, north-mini-code-1.0 scores J under 20% in 5 of the 9 modes it ran in, Phi-4-mini scores J under 20% in 6 of the 8 modes it ran in and grok-4.1-fast flags more than 30% of clean samples in 6 of 9 modes. The other models that ran in at least 8 modes (gpt-6-luna, deepseek-v4-flash, mimo-v2.6-flash, claude-fable-5-2, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-haiku-5-5) score J under 20% in at most 2 modes and flag more than 30% of clean samples in at most 2.
<!-- END saica-bench results -->

## Where things are in this repository

- `bench/`: one folder per failure mode (runners, scoring, notes). `bench/<mode>/published/` holds the tracked scores and per-sample verdicts; `bench/build_report.py` builds `site/public/bench/results.json`, the published results, from them. Datasets and raw model answers are not in git.
- `data/`: SAICA-KG, one YAML file per node (tools, failure modes, papers, incidents, taxonomies, crosswalks, recipes); the ids are listed in `data/MANIFEST.json`, removed ids in `data/TOMBSTONES.yml`. Schemas in `schema/`; validate with `.venv/bin/python validator/cli.py`. A tool's failure-mode tag is the tool's claim, not a measurement.
- `site/`: the Astro site served at https://saica.ai; `pipeline/webapp.py` serves the built site plus the `/api/ask`, `/api/assess`, `/api/health` endpoints.
- `requirements/`: one dependency list per use, with pinned versions in `constraints.txt`.
- `README.md`: overview, current results and the development commands; `CITATION.cff`: how to cite; `LICENSE-DATA`: data licences by source.
